question: In March 2025, which country hosted the G20 Foreign Ministers' meeting?
solution:
The correct answer is __**South Africa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **G20 Foreign Ministers Meeting**: The G20 comprises 19 countries and the European Union, representing the world's largest economies. The foreign ministers of these nations meet periodically to discuss global issues, including diplomacy, trade, and security.
 
• In **March 2025**, the meeting of the **G20 Foreign Ministers** is hosted by **South Africa**, one of the member countries of the G20 group.
 
• **South Africa's Role in G20:** South Africa is the only African country in the G20 and plays a pivotal role in representing the continent's interests on global platforms. This hosting opportunity underscores South Africa’s significance in international diplomacy.
 
• **Agenda of the Meeting:** G20 Foreign Ministers' Meetings generally focus on issues like **global economic recovery, climate change, sustainable development, and international security**. South Africa's hosting likely emphasizes African concerns such as **socio-economic development, health, and climate resilience**.
 
• **Previous G20 Meetings:** The presidency of G20 rotates among member countries annually. South Africa hosting the foreign ministers' meeting highlights its active participation and leadership in global discussions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About G20:**

 
 
• The **Group of Twenty (G20)** was established in **1999** as an international forum for governments and central bank governors from 19 countries and the European Union.
 
• It includes major economies such as **the USA, China, India, Germany, Japan, and South Africa**, among others, representing about **80% of the global GDP** and **75% of international trade**.
 
• The G20's objective is to address issues related to the global economy, such as **financial stability, climate change, and sustainable development**.
 
 
 
• **South Africa’s Membership:**
 
 
• South Africa joined the G20 in **2008** and has consistently advocated for equitable global policies that benefit developing nations.
 
• As the only African member, South Africa often focuses on **poverty alleviation, health systems strengthening, and climate adaptation** in Africa.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Hosting:**
 
 
• Hosting a G20 meeting signifies a nation's ability to lead global conversations and showcases its diplomatic strength.
 
• For South Africa, this reinforces its position as a voice for developing countries and a leader in promoting **regional cooperation** within Africa.
 
 
 
• **Recent G20 Presidency:**
 
 
• The G20 presidency rotates annually among its members. Recent presidencies include **India (2023)**, **Indonesia (2022)**, and **Italy (2021)**.
 
• South Africa's hosting of the foreign ministers' meeting aligns with its active role in global governance and economic discussions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **South Africa’s Global Diplomacy:**

 
 
• South Africa is a member of several international organizations, including **BRICS, the African Union, and the United Nations**.
 
• Its active diplomacy is aimed at fostering **peace, security, and development** on the African continent and globally.
 
 
 
• **Key Agenda Items for Africa:**
 
 
• As host, South Africa is likely to focus on issues such as **poverty reduction, access to vaccines, climate resilience, and sustainable infrastructure**.
 
• The meeting provides an opportunity to highlight **Africa’s developmental needs** on a global platform.
 
 
 
• **Global Economic Recovery:**
 
 
• The G20 continues to address challenges posed by the **COVID-19 pandemic**, including vaccine distribution and economic recovery.
 
• South Africa’s hosting emphasizes equitable solutions for **developing countries**.
